name: AND Graph
description: You are given a set of size $$$m$$$ with integer elements between $$$0$$$ and $$$2^{n}-1$$$ inclusive. Let's build an undirected graph on these integers in the following way: connect two integers $$$x$$$ and $$$y$$$ with an edge if and only if $$$x \& y = 0$$$. Here $$$\&$$$ is the bitwise AND operation . Count the number of connected components in that graph.
input_specification: In the first line of input there are two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$0 \le n \le 22$$$, $$$1 \le m \le 2^{n}$$$). In the second line there are $$$m$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_m$$$ ($$$0 \le a_{i} \lt 2^{n}$$$) — the elements of the set. All $$$a_{i}$$$ are distinct.
output_specification: Print the number of connected components.
approach_summary: Maintain disjoint sets using path compression and union by rank/size. Process edge additions and component queries in O(α(N)) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 986C — AND Graph [80. DSU / Union Find]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Connectivity is an equivalence relation. By organizing connected components into trees and merging smaller trees into larger ones (`union-by-rank/size`) combined with path compression, find and union operations run in near-constant inverse Ackermann time $O(\alpha(N))$.
